This judgement shall dispose of petition filed on behalf of the petitioner Under section 13(1)(ia) of Hindu Marriage Act seeking dissolution of marriage by a decree of divorce and application u/s 24 of Hindu Marriage Act filed by the respondent/wife (hereinafter referred to as Act), as per the orders of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India dated 22.07.2011 in Transfer Petition (Civil) Nos. 13241325 of 2008. 2. Facts giving rise to the present petition,in brief, are that petitioner was married to respondent on 05.07.1995 at Shiv Puri, Madhya Pradesh. At the time of marriage, the petitioner was working as Vitreo Ratina fellow in Shankar Eye Hospital and also in Sita Pur Eye Hospital, Sita Pur from July, 1996 to December, 1997 and thereafter, he was posted in Sita Pur Eye Hospital, Bareilly from January, 1998 to July,1999. From August, 1999 onwards, he has been in medical practice. It has been further averred in the petition that at present he was practising in District Bareilly as a surgeon in Kesh Lata Hospital and also as Assistant Professor in Ruhel Khand Medical College, Bareilly. Since 1995, both the parties resided together at different places and from January, 1998, they started residing within the jurisdiction of P S Bareilly. Out of the wedlock, three children, two daughters, namely, Kriti, Suchi Gupta and son Paritosh were born. It is further stated that petitioner was living separately in Bareilly from his parents, brothers and sisters since January, 1998. The respondent was having relations with bad elements of society and her behaviour towards the petitioner was very cruel, she always misbehaved with him and never allowed him to live peacefully which was very essential for him as he was an eye surgeon. He further stated that for the last six R K Gupta vs Varsha Gupta on 7 June, 2014 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166761209/ 1 months, he was compelled to stay in his clinic at 84C, Civil Lines, Bareilly and arranging meals from hotel. He bore all the educational expenses of his children. He also purchased one expensive flat in Priyadarshini Nagar, Bareilly in December, 2004 in joint name with his wife. 3. It has been further pleaded in the petition that respondent used to blackmail him and demanded Rs.40 lacs to agree for divorce and misbehaved with him alongwith one Sushma Arora, President of Shakti Vahini who was also demanding Rs.5 lacs from him. The behaviour of the respondent has been very cruel towards the petitioner since the very inception of the marriage and she also refused to have matrimonial relations or cohabitation with him due to which he suffered great mental agony and shock and he realised that it was not possible for him to live with the respondent as she will blackmail him and could also falsely implicate him in dowry cases which will affect his social status. The petitioner was deprived of marital bliss and was forced to live outside his house due to which he suffered great mental pain and agony, as a result, he filed the present divorce petition against the respondent. The respondent also filed one written complaint against the petitioner before SSP, Bareilly on 23.04.2007. The petitioner decided to file the present divorce petition because of the incident which took place on the afternoon of 23.04.2007 when respondent abused him, misbehaved with him and demanded Rs.40lacs for separation and also threatened him to falsely implicate him in a dowry case and day by day the behaviour of respondent became cruel towards him. He further stated that the respondent filed a number of complaints against him to disgrace him in his medical profession and to defame him in the society. The respondent lodged false complaints regarding dowry demand before the police authority, which, after investigation were found to be totally false. After having lived with him for continuous twelve years and having all luxuries of life, now the behaviour of the respondent/wife turned very cruel and humiliating which caused grave mental pain and stress to him. He further stated that police official Sameer Saurabh, police official of Bareilly, conducted investigation into the complaints of the respondent and filed his written report dated 17.05.2007 indicating that respondent/wife wanted to ruin the life of the petitioner and her sole objective was to send him behind the bars. There is no other way to live peacefully but to get divorce from the respondent/wife. The petitioner also got registered one FIR against the respondent and her friend Sushma Arora. The petitioner tried to reconcile the matter with his wife/respondent, after institution of petition u/s 10 of Hindu Marriage Act and tried to make her understand to change her behaviour, he also used to visit the house to give household expenses but at that time also, the respondent treated him with cruelty and never asked him for tea or food etc but abused him and used filthy language against his other family members which also caused mental trauma and agony to him. He further stated that as per the call details of the respondent for the month of March/April, 2007, the respondent used to make long calls to her family and friends and always planned to send him behind bars and to falsely implicate him. He further stated that relation of husband and wife are very intimate relations and when there is no faith in that relationship and when the wife used to call Press Conferences to defame him with false complaints, as a result, it became very difficult to live with such kind of life partner. He further stated that respondent is in the habit of threatening him to call the police on one pretext or the other and never tried to reconcile the matter, so, it is not possible for the petitioner to live with the respondent any more. In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, it is prayed that the petition filed under Section 13 (1)(ia) of Hindu Marriage Act be allowed and decree of divorce be passed in favour of the petitioner.
